questions.prompt: A vLLM Deployment has an HPA on CPU at 70%. During a traffic spike, time to first token rises from 0.3 s to 40 s while `kubectl get hpa` shows `cpu: 31%/70%`. Why does it not scale?
choices: The HPA's 15-second sync period is too long to see the spike
metrics-server cannot read the CPU of pods that use a GPU
The HPA ignores pods that request an extended resource such as nvidia.com/gpu
The pod's CPU is mostly one engine loop that is busy as soon as anything runs; waiting requests add almost no CPU, so utilisation plateaus below the target while the queue grows
questions.explanation: Decode is bound by GPU memory bandwidth and concurrency by KV capacity; neither shows up in pod CPU. The queue is visible only in the server's own metrics: vllm:num_requests_waiting, llamacpp:requests_deferred or sglang:num_queue_reqs.

questions.prompt: Three ready vLLM replicas report running + waiting of 10, 14 and 12. The HPA has an AverageValue target of 4 per replica and the default behavior. What does it set this period?
choices: 9, because ceil(36 / 4) = 9
3, because each replica is still within its batch limit
7: the raw recommendation is 9, but the default scale-up policy allows at most doubling or four more pods per 15 s, whichever is more, so 9 comes a period later if the load holds
12, one replica per three requests
questions.explanation: desired = ceil(total / target) = 9, the ratio 36 / (3 x 4) = 3 is far outside the 0.1 tolerance, and the scale-up limit from 3 is max(6, 7) = 7. infscale prints the same three steps.

questions.prompt: Load stops at 10:00. With the default HPA behavior, the last recommendation above 1 was 6, at 09:58. When can the Deployment go back to 1 replica?
choices: Around 10:03: scale-down goes only to the highest recommendation in the last 300 s, and the 6 from 09:58 stays in that window until then
At the next 15-second sync after the queue empties
After KEDA's cooldownPeriod, which applies to every scale-down
Never: the HPA does not scale below the peak it reached
questions.explanation: The scale-down stabilisation window keeps the maximum of the stored recommendations. KEDA's cooldownPeriod applies only to the last step from 1 to 0; between 1 and N the HPA that KEDA generates decides, under its own window.

questions.prompt: A KEDA ScaledObject scales a vLLM Deployment on the Prometheus query `sum(vllm:num_requests_waiting)` with minReplicaCount 0. It scales to zero overnight and never comes back in the morning, although clients are sending requests. Why?
choices: cooldownPeriod is shorter than pollingInterval

At zero there is no vLLM pod, so Prometheus scrapes nothing, the query returns no value and the trigger never becomes active; the waking demand has to be counted in front of the pods, by the KEDA HTTP add-on's interceptor, a gateway or Knative's activator
activationThreshold has to be negative for the trigger to fire
The HPA that KEDA created still has minReplicas 1 and blocks the change
questions.explanation: A metric exported by the pods disappears with them. Scale to zero needs a component that outlives the pods, holds the request and reports it as demand, which is the held argument in infscale's decision.

questions.prompt: A replica needs 90 s from scale-up to Ready. Traffic ramps from 10 to 30 requests per second within a minute, and one replica serves about 13. Which change does most for time-to-first-token misses during the ramp?
choices: A longer scale-down stabilisation window
Scaling earlier, with a target below the replica's knee or a lookahead over the cold start, and shortening the cold start itself with pre-pulled images and locally cached weights
Switching the metric to KV cache usage
A higher maxReplicas
questions.explanation: During the cold start the queue grows by arrivals minus capacity times 90 s, all of it on the replicas you already have. Only headroom bought before the ramp, or a shorter cold start, prevents that; the window and maxReplicas change nothing during the ramp.

questions.prompt: Why does infscale refuse `--metric cpu --min 0` with exit code 2?
choices: KEDA's cooldownPeriod does not apply to CPU triggers
CPU utilisation never drops to zero, so the idle cooldown would never start
With no pod there is no CPU sample, so a utilisation metric can never produce the first replica; only demand counted outside the pods, such as held requests, can wake a service from zero
A CPU target must be at least 50% for scale to zero to be stable
questions.explanation: A utilisation metric is an average over the pods that report it. At zero pods that average does not exist, which is also why the HPA allows minReplicas 0 only behind a feature gate and only for Object or External metrics.
